record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.context_brief: local structure of BV Euler solutions
record.original_question: Suppose V(x,t) is a BV weak solution of the full compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid satisfying the physical entropy condition. What additional local structure must V(x,t) have in physical space beyond merely belonging to BV, and can it be described locally as an appropriate perturbation of a Riemann solution or even as a viscosity solution in the sense of Bressan?

evidence.quote: Local structures of solutions in BV space. Let V(x,t) ∈ BV be a weak solution to the full Euler equations of polytropic fluids satisfying the physical entropy condition. What are the additional local structures of V(x,t) in the physical space beyond those of a BV functions [26]? Can V(x,t) behave locally as an appropriate perturbation of a Riemann solutions as Glimm solutions do? In particular, can V(x,t) be an viscosity solution in the sense of [8]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional full compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid:
   ρ_t + (ρu)_x = 0,
   (ρu)_t + (ρu^2 + p)_x = 0,
   (ρE)_t + (u(ρE + p))_x = 0,
where ρ > 0 is density, u is velocity, E = e + u^2/2 is total specific energy, e is specific internal energy, and the equation of state is that of a polytropic gas, p = (γ−1)ρe with adiabatic exponent γ > 1, and the temperature/entropy is determined accordingly. Let V(x,t) = (ρ,u,E)(x,t) be a weak solution of this system in the sense of distributions, with V ∈ BV_loc (functions of locally bounded variation in (x,t)), satisfying the physical (Clausius–Duhem) entropy inequality
   (ρS)_t + (ρuS)_x ≥ 0
in the sense of distributions, where S is the thermodynamic specific entropy.

Question: What additional local structural properties must V(x,t) possess in (x,t)-space beyond those guaranteed by membership in BV alone? In particular:
(a) Around almost every point (x_0, t_0), can V be described locally as a suitable perturbation of a self-similar Riemann solution (i.e., does V locally look like the solution to a Riemann problem with constant left/right states, in the sense established for Glimm-type front-tracking solutions)?
(b) Is every such V necessarily a viscosity solution in the Bianchini–Bressan sense, i.e., obtainable as the limit, as ε → 0+, of solutions V^ε to the parabolic regularization V^ε_t + F(V^ε)_x = ε V^ε_{xx}?

Provide either a proof that every BV entropy solution admits such a local structure / viscosity-solution characterization, or a counterexample.
artifact.category_tag: BV solutions of compressible Euler equations
artifact.status_search_result: The fine local structure of BV entropy solutions to the full compressible Euler equations, and whether they coincide with vanishing-viscosity (Bianchini–Bressan) solutions, remains a recognized open problem. Bianchini–Bressan (2005) established the viscosity-solution theory for small-BV solutions of general strictly hyperbolic systems with artificial viscosity, but the corresponding theory for physical viscosity (Navier–Stokes) and the local Riemann-type structure for general BV entropy solutions of the full Euler system are still open.

status_evidence.title: Large solutions for compressible Euler equations (G. Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of large BV solutions for the initial value problems to 1-D isentropic and full Euler equations is a notoriously difficult and important open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Large-BV theory and structural results for full Euler remain open.

status_evidence.title: Inviscid limits of compressible Navier-Stokes to small BV solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Bianchini-Bressan (2005) obtained small BV solutions as inviscid limits with artificial viscosity; whether this holds for physical regularizations is an important open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Viscosity-solution characterization in the Bressan sense for physical regularizations is open.
